accuracy.evidence: Checked CCSS 1.NBT.2a–c: two digits as tens and ones; teens as 1 ten + ones; decades as tens + 0 ones; value 10×tens+ones.

misconceptions.evidence: Checked traps: digit-sum (47 as 11); reversed places (47 as 7 tens); tens digit read as that many ones; teen as 1+4=5.

lab_distinct.evidence: Checked flag2digit: place-chart build + digit expansion; not flagbundle (10 ones↔1 ten swap), flagtenten (hundreds), flagdigit (glyphs), flagteens alone.

lab_teaches.evidence: Checked: learner builds 35, expands 47, names tens-digit worth, expands 14, spots digit-sum myth, builds 52.

predictions.evidence: Checked tempting wrongs on 35 value, 47 expansion, tens-digit worth, teen expansion, digit-sum myth, and 52 build.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked why() splits digit-sum, reversed places, tens-read-as-ones, and true place-value statements marked ok.

readability.evidence: Checked ages 6–7 kid lines use tens / ones / expand; adult names CCSS 1.NBT.2 and common slips within family bars.

no_filler.evidence: Checked every sentence teaches place value, expansion, teen/decade structure, or a named mix-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked place-chart Add ten/Add one buttons and large choice lbtns; layout holds near 390 px width.

accessibility.evidence: Checked Add-ten/Add-one and expansion buttons twin canvas taps; live aria-label tracks the place chart; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: CCSS 1.NBT.2 Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones
UK NC 2013 Maths Y2 recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones)
